outcome: severity of wheezing attacks (hospitalization, oxygen therapy, steroid therapy)
cohort: The study included 52 patients aged 12-60 months with a history of three or more wheezing attacks in the last year and 54 healthy control children.
finding: Children with recurrent wheezing had significantly lower serum vitamin D levels compared to healthy controls, and other identified risk factors included cigarette exposure, breastfeeding for six months or less, humid home environment, and family history of allergic disease.
mod_finding: A history of cesarean section was significantly higher in the patient group compared with the control group, suggesting it might be a risk factor for recurrent wheezing.
cross-section timing: Children were recruited based on current wheezing status or as healthy controls, and data on their current physiological levels and historical risk factors were collected.
